sampled_review.note: No sampled review has run, so there is no pass rate. This field previously read 1.0 against n of 0, which made regression_rule.thresholds.sampled_review_pass_rate_min unable to ever fire. A null rate means the threshold is not evaluable, not that it passed.

evidence.period: 2026-08. 45 v1 baseline runs, 45 v2 runs after the routing and oracle corrections, and 18 timing-ablation runs on 2026-08-03.

authorisation_note: Authorised on 2026-08-02, one day before the benchmark it cites as evidence. The evidence block was back-filled on 2026-08-03. The authorisation is not re-dated, because re-dating it would hide that ordering; it is recorded instead. The level rests on the 2026-08-03 batch and has not been reauthorised since. The benchmark was rebuilt and re-run on 2026-08-08, and ADR-0007 makes that batch the final measured state of the line and stops any further runs, so a reauthorisation against it is a reading the operator can take whenever he wants and no run is waiting to be made. This record decides three things: level, expires and regression_rule. It used to restate the test-timing defaults the ablation set, which is a fact that already lives in kernel/templates/org/TESTING.tpl.md and in packs/delivery-testing/PACK.md; that copy was cut on 2026-08-10 under T-0018 so the defaults have one writer. Nothing loads this file; it is read by a person following test_timing per-profile from org/policy.json, and both the TESTING template and the delivery-testing pack point here.

regression_rule.not_evaluable_reason: sampled_review.n is 0, so sampled_review_pass_rate_min has nothing to test. The rule fires on escaped_defects only until a sampled review runs.
